text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- American Express stopped sales of travelers' cheques in Bulgaria after the country's central bank filed insolvency suits against another eight commercial banks on October 31 and the International Monetary Fund proposed introduction of a currency board system, AmEx officials in Sofia said. @

-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency (PA) has received guarantees from a first-rate foreign bank for payments by the U.S. General Chemical Group Inc., which was announced as a winner in a tender for a 60 percent stake in Bulgaria's Sodi Devnya chemical company, PA director Vesselin Blagoev said.

-- A third round for the selloff of 60 percent of Bulgaria's Sodi Devnya chemical company might be held because details of offers made by tender bidders are considered confidential before the sale contract is signed, experts said. @
Bulgaria's deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev announced on Thursday that the tender was won by the U.S. General Chemical Group Inc. with an offer of $160 million.

-- The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) has sold government securities worth 4.362 billion levs from its treasury portfolio in the first two weeks of November, bringing the total amount of paper in its portfolio to 75.975 billion levs on November 15, BNB statistics showed.

-- Bank deposits of Bulgarians in foreign currency rose by an equivelent of 2.90 billion levs in the second week of November because of an anticipated fall of the lev against the dollar and lower-than-inflation interest rates on lev deposits, BNB figures showed.

-- Eight companies are interested in the privatisation of Bulgaria's Chimko Vratsa chemical fertiliser maker and proceeds from the sale are expected at some 25 billion levs, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
-- The governing Socialist party (BSP) could submit to parliament a proposal for the introduction of a currency board system in Bulgaria in three months at the earliest, a senior BSP official said.
The currency board scheme was proposed by the International Monetary Fund to help restore confidence in the lev, defeat hyperinflation and boost economic growth. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
